findings.quote: Find the slope of $3x=12$ and the slope of $2y=6$. State whether the two lines are perpendicular.
findings.problem: The example requires the meaning of perpendicular, but this part never defines it as meeting at a right angle or points to a lesson that does. The solution states that vertical and horizontal lines are perpendicular without explaining the term.
findings.source: content-checklist.md, L25; lesson-style-guide.md, Teaching completeness; [OpenStax Elementary Algebra 2e, §4.5](https://openstax.org/books/elementary-algebra-2e/pages/4-5-use-the-slope-intercept-form-of-an-equation-of-a-line).

findings.quote: 1. Read the given line's slope from standard form.
findings.problem: The solution obtains -2/5 from 2x+5y=10 without teaching the standard-form slope rule m=-A/B or showing how to isolate y. The rule is taught in line-slopes-and-intercepts.md, but this part provides no prerequisite reference.
findings.source: content-checklist.md, L17 and L26; lesson-style-guide.md, Teaching completeness; [OpenStax Elementary Algebra 2e, §4.5](https://openstax.org/books/elementary-algebra-2e/pages/4-5-use-the-slope-intercept-form-of-an-equation-of-a-line).

findings.problem: The solution needs the two-point slope formula and slope-intercept form to obtain the boundary equation. This part teaches neither method and does not point to line-slopes-and-intercepts.md, where they are taught.
